sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Tipton County?
sections.html:
Three separate offices touch a Tipton County tax bill. The Assessor, Will Carter, values every parcel. The county commission and each city council set rates. The Trustee mails the bills and takes the money. The Assessor's own page lists three things the office does not do: it does not set the rate, send bills or collect taxes.

The Trustee works from 1 Pleasant Avenue, Room 203, in Covington (mailing address PO Box 487, Covington, TN 38019), phone 901-476-0211, weekdays 8:00 to 5:00. During tax season a second counter opens at Munford City Hall, 1397 Munford Avenue, every Wednesday from the first Wednesday in October through February 24, 2027, with Veterans Day and December 23 skipped. Questions about value or a mailing address go to the Assessor at 901-476-0213, the number the City of Covington gives on its tax page.

City tax is separate. The Trustee's page says city taxes are not collected at the county counter, and it lists the municipal offices:

  • Covington, 200 W Washington Avenue, 901-476-9613
  • Atoka, 334 Atoka-Munford Avenue, 901-837-5300
  • Brighton, 1270 Old Highway 51 S, 901-476-8661
  • Mason, 12157 Main Street, 901-294-3525
  • Munford, 1397 Munford Avenue, 901-837-0171

Covington says its own tax is due October 1 and delinquent March 1, with no partial payments, and quotes a city rate of $1.0128 per $100 of assessed value. A Covington house therefore carries a county bill and a city bill.

sections.h2: What is Tipton County like, and why does it matter for a tax bill?
sections.html:
Tipton County sits on the western edge of Tennessee, with the Mississippi River as its western boundary and Covington as the county seat. It covers 473 square miles, was formed on October 29, 1823 from part of Shelby County, and belongs to the Memphis metropolitan area. U.S. Highway 51 runs north to south through Covington. The county also lies on the southeastern edge of the New Madrid Seismic Zone, which Wikipedia notes as an area of high earthquake risk.

Towns inside the county are Atoka, Brighton, Burlison, Garland, Gilt Edge and Mason, plus the cities of Covington and Munford. Covington's South Main Historic District holds about 50 homes from the late 1800s and early 1900s, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Tipton County:

  • 62,287 residents in July 2025, up 2.2% from the April 2020 base
  • 25,033 housing units, with 76.3% owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024
  • Median owner-occupied home value of $240,600, and median gross rent of $1,013
  • Median household income of $74,127, with a mean commute of 32.9 minutes
  • 139 building permits issued in 2025

sections.h2: How is a Tipton County tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The Assessor sets an appraised value, the state assessment ratio turns that into assessed value, and the rate is applied per $100. The Assessor's page gives the ratios: residential 25 percent, farm 25 percent, commercial and industrial 40 percent, personal property 30 percent, public utility 55 percent.

Take a house appraised at $200,000. At 25 percent the assessed value is $50,000. At the 2026 rate of $1.3417 per $100, the county bill comes to roughly $671. At the 2025 rate of $1.5217 the same house would have owed about $761. The rate has fallen steadily in the history the Trustee posts:

Tipton County is on a six-year reappraisal cycle: five years of on-site review of every parcel, then a revaluation in the sixth year. Ask the Assessor which year of the cycle the county is in, since a revaluation year is when values on a house tend to move most.

sections.h2: When is Tipton County property tax due, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
Taxes are due from the first Monday in October, and the county allows payment without interest through February 28. The bill becomes delinquent on March 1. Interest of 1.5 percent is added on the first day of each month from March 1, rounded to the nearest dollar. The Trustee posts the running total: 1.5 percent in March, 3.0 in April, 4.5 in May, and so on up to 18.0 percent in February and 19.5 in the following March.

The notice goes out in the first week of October to the person who owned the property on January 1. If a deed is recorded before the September deadline, a second notice goes to the new owner. Today is November 15, 2026, so the 2026 bill is open and no interest has started. Ways to pay include:

  • In person at the Covington counter or the Wednesday Munford counter
  • Online through the Trustee's payment portal, which charges 2.5 percent on a card or $1.25 on an online check
  • By phone at 1-855-548-3603, which adds a $0.30 processing fee on top of the same service charges
  • By bank draft, offered as one annual payment, four payments from November through February, or monthly; call 901-476-0211

Partial payments are taken at the Trustee's office, but any balance left after February 28 collects interest. Refunds are only issued on a parcel that another agency, such as a lender, has already paid. The Trustee states no refund is made for any other reason.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Tipton County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor, then the County Board of Equalization. The Assessor opens the roll for public inspection in May and mails notices to owners whose values changed. Owners who think a value is above fair market value can ask the county board to hear it. The board's decision makes the roll final for the year.

The state process picks up from there. A disputed assessment generally has to reach the county board first, or it becomes final. An owner who disagrees with the county board can appeal to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date the county board's notice was sent, whichever is later. For tax year 2026 the August 1 date has passed, so check the notice date. The state's guidance on evidence points to:

  • Sales of comparable homes, with differences in size, age, condition and location explained
  • An appraisal, where the appraiser may be asked to testify
  • A stated value and the reason for it, since a bare claim of overvaluation is usually not enough

Pay at least the undisputed part of the bill before March 1 to avoid interest, along with any earlier-year delinquent tax. The State Board's scheduling line is 615-401-7883.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Tipton County?
sections.html:
The state Tax Relief Program reimburses part or all of the tax paid by low-income elderly and disabled homeowners, and by disabled veterans and widows or widowers of disabled veterans. The Trustee lists the 2026 income cap as $38,470 from all sources for the applicant, spouse and other owners, counted on 2025 income. The state says the program has run since 1973. Relief is a payment back to the owner, so the bill still has to be paid first.

Elderly applicants bring proof of 2025 income and a Medicare or Social Security card. Disabled applicants add proof of age and a benefits letter if the benefits do not come from Social Security. Veterans sign an F-16 and show ID. Anyone in a mobile home brings the title, bill of sale or an affidavit of affixation. Call 901-476-0211 to start, since applications for 2026 open in October.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Tipton County house sells?
sections.html: The January 1 owner is on the roll, so a house sold in the fall still carries a bill in the seller's name. At closing the title company normally splits the year, and the buyer takes over from there. A seller with unpaid tax should ask the Trustee for the exact payoff, including any interest, before setting a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the Tipton County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county rate for 2026 is $1.3417 per $100 of assessed value, down from $1.5217 in 2025. City tax is billed separately, and Covington lists $1.0128 per $100.

faqs.q: When are Tipton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due from the first Monday in October and can be paid without interest through February 28. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts on March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Tipton County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Trustee's office at 1 Pleasant Avenue, Room 203, in Covington, or on Wednesdays at Munford City Hall during tax season. Online, phone and bank draft payments are also offered by the Trustee.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of Tipton County property tax?
faqs.a: Only on a parcel that another agency has already paid, such as a lender. The Trustee says refunds are not issued for any other reason.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Tipton County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Property Assessor at 901-476-0213. The Assessor can review a value and explain how to reach the County Board of Equalization.
